SMTO-SKL-0169 — SMTO couldn't find that pull request

GUID: d37eb860-7d61-50e4-883b-5bc1f825d479
Slug: github-pull-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub says the pull request, or part of it such as its reviews, isn't in this repository. GitHub also says this when your token isn't allowed to see it. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the pull request on github.com, check its number and repository, and repeat your request with both. Pull request numbers belong to one repository; a fork has its own numbers.
  2. On github.com, check that your token has read access to Pull requests for this repository. GitHub hides pull requests a token can't read, so they look missing.
  3. If you changed the token's permissions, update the granted permissions in your GitHub account entry in Parameter Store and select Save. SMTO checks the permissions recorded there before contacting GitHub.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the pull request's title and details when you ask about it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume the pull request was deleted; it may only be hidden from your token.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A pull-request operation (including review, file, commit or comment resources) received HTTP 404 from GitHub in the resolved repository; GitHub may return 404 for inaccessible private resources.

What this means

  • A pull-prefixed operation receives HTTP 404, including related review resources. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • A pull-prefixed operation receives HTTP 404, including related review resources.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify PR number, related resource ID and Pull requests permission in the exact repository.

How to fix it

  • GitHubService.dispatch maps 404 for pull* operations to pull_not_found with may_be_inaccessible=true. Verify the PR number in the exact owner/repo and that the PAT has pull_requests:read for that repository (and organization/SSO approval where required); 404 does not prove absence.
  • Verify the PR number in the exact repository and Pull requests read permission; 404 can mean inaccessible.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended PR resource is visible under the selected account.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
